chunks.text: Now we're going to look at something called daily returns.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Daily returns are one of the most important statistics used in financial analysis.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: So let's consider first here this time series S&P 500 in 2012.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: What daily returns are is simply how much did the price go up or

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: down on a particular day.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: So for instance, on this day it went down a little,

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: on the next day it went up a lot.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Daily returns are calculated easily using a simple equation here.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: So the daily return for day t, let's say today,

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: is simply today's stock price divided by yesterday's stock price minus 1.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Let me show you an example.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Let's suppose on this particular day,

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: the price went from $100 yesterday to $110 today.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: The daily return then for that day is 110 divided by 100 minus 1 or 1.1 minus 1 equals 0.1,

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: which is 10%.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: So that's how we calculate daily returns.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Now one thing to remember is this is a kind of statement you might put in a for loop

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: where you iterate over individual days.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Don't do that.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Use the numpy syntax we showed you where you can do this in a single statement with no for loops.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Here's what a chart for daily returns might look like.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Everything is scaled now from minus 10% to plus 10%.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: And what we see here is a daily return for each day.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: If it was a positive return, of course, it's positive and negative if it were negative.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Remember that day when we calculated we had a positive return of 10%?

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: That corresponds to that point right here.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: And for instance, here on the next day we had negative daily return.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: That corresponds to that point right here.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Key thing to remember here is this is a line that sort of zigs and zags, usually close to 0.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: And if you were to say take the mean of all these values, because we've had a generally upward moving trend here,

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: our mean would probably be a little bit positive above 0.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: Where looking at daily returns can be really important and revealing is to compare daily returns

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: between different stocks or different assets.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: So for example, we might compare how Exxon moves in comparison to S&P 500.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: As one example, if you take a look at this section here, you can see that when S&P 500 went up, Exxon went down.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: And that's revealed here in this section of the daily returns.

chunks.title: Daily returns
chunks.text: We're going to spend a lot of time in some future lessons looking at how these statistics,
